History Channel: Battle for the Pacific came out in 2007 for PC, Xbox 360, PS2, PS3 and Wii. The game is an FPS. It was developed by Cauldron HQ and produced by Activision Value. I got the game for $10 on amazon for PS3. The game is around $5 at most other places.

For the story, it follows a few battles over the course of the Pacific during World War 2 which covers from Wake Island to Iwo Jima.

The main campaign takes about 2-3hrs to beat. It's pretty annoying to play through since you have to follow the sergeant the entire game. If you get to far away from him, its game over. However, he gets stuck a lot, forcing you to run far ahead of him to try to make him become unstuck, or reload the level if that doesn't work.

The controllers are very stiff making it hard to aim, but thankfully the enemies drop pretty fast and they all drop in the same exact pose every time they die. The only entertaining thing is watching enemies fly around when you hit them with grenades.

Overall the game just sucks, and it isn't worth the money for it. I give it a 3/10. Thankfully, this is the last game in the History Channel series. At least until WW3 happens.
